title: Frame drops on phones in my three.js browser game. Here's what I've tried so far. What would you do next?
author: Perfect-Builder4321
selftext:
I'm a solo dev making a pixel beat 'em up that runs in the browser (built with a lot of AI help for art and code). It's 2D pixel sprites on billboards in a three.js scene, with shadows, depth of field, bloom and fog on top. Hit effects and damage numbers are drawn on 2D canvases and uploaded as textures every frame.



On PC it runs smoothly. On my phone, busy fights dropped frames badly and the phone got hot. Here's what I've done so far:



**Rendering**

\- Touch devices (\`pointer: coarse\`) render the 3D scene at max 720p and upscale. On a small screen I honestly can't see the difference.

\- A "lite" effects mode on touch devices: DOF samples 16 → 8, bloom at half resolution, shadow map 2048 → 1024.

\- Cap at 60 fps on phones. 120Hz screens were drawing twice as many frames and the GPU never got a break. There's also a battery saver option that caps at 30.



**The surprise costs (found with Chrome DevTools, CPU throttled 4x)**

\- Uploading the effects canvas (1160×360) as a texture took about 8 ms, half the frame budget. Fix: no \`willReadFrequently\`, \`flipY = false\` (flip the UVs instead) and \`premultiplyAlpha = true\`, so the copy can stay on the GPU.

\- Layout thrashing: I was reading \`offsetWidth\` / \`clientWidth\` every frame right after updating HUD elements, which forced a full layout each time. Now I only read sizes when something changes (ResizeObserver).

\- Setting \`ctx.font\` every draw call, even when it didn't change. Now only when it does.

\- I added a \`?fps\` overlay that shows FPS, worst frame time, update vs. draw time, draw calls and texture count, so I can check on the phone itself.



It's better now, but I'm sure there's more. What I'd love to hear:

\- Is drawing effects on a 2D canvas and re-uploading every frame just a bad idea? Should hit effects and numbers be real sprites / instanced meshes instead?

\- Do you use dynamic resolution (drop the render scale when frame time goes up) or a fixed setting per device?

\- Which post-processing would you cut first on mobile: shadows, DOF or bloom?

\- How do you deal with thermal throttling on longer play sessions?

\- How do you test on low-end Android without a drawer full of phones?

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
Ask it what stuff is being rendered every frame,  ask it to make it so that if stuff is static and un changing that it should not be re-rendered. only stuff that changes needs to be re-rendered. (ai does this all the time)

ask it to turn all hud and overlay elements into images instead of using expensive kinds of rendering.

Cull anything outside the view area. the ai will not automatically do this and will sometimes just leave stuff rendering when you can't see it.

panel based render buckets, you can divide stuff into chunks and render them rather than going pixel by pixel which can help. too.

get your current render system as a overview from your ai,  copy and paste this to another ai like gemini and ask it where you could improve the framerate.

replies.author: Perfect-Builder4321
replies.body: Thanks! Most of these were already in — dirty-flag uploads for effect layers, three.js frustum culling, a DOM HUD. Profiling the phone showed the real cost was full-screen post-processing (DOF/bloom), so I lowered the render resolution on phones, capped it at 60fps and added a Battery Saver mode. Your first point did catch one thing, though: the paused screen was still re-rendering every frame. Fixing that next

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
yah dem AI is sneaky lol. mine keeps sneaking in the every frame im gunna do this.

But yeah post processing is a big hit, it depends what exactly you are putting in. dont forget like depending on how you have it working it might be re-rendering everything under your transparant clouds, fog and things more than one time for like each layer of transparancy.  which is another invisible sink for frames.

replies.author: Perfect-Builder4321
replies.body:
Ha, yes. "I'll just recompute this every frame" shows up way too often.

Good point on transparency. My fog is the built-in distance fog, so no extra layer there, but I do stack a few full-width transparent planes (two effect layers, background layers, a haze plane in some valley stages) on top of the sprites. On a phone GPU that overdraw could easily add up. I'll toggle them one by one with the fps overlay and see which one hurts.

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
a cheap method is to merge your transparancies into one layer, this works well for the shadows from clouds,  that way you dont get any overlap shading between and they look more natural and flowwy :)

https://i.redd.it/dnyw9vzl912i1.gif

ive got both kinds of fog and clouds on this one,  some overlapping ground foggles and  larger clouds that operate on a single layer.

replies.author: Perfect-Builder4321
replies.body:
That's a nice trick. Merging them also gets rid of the darker patches where two shadows overlap, so it helps the look and the cost at the same time.

Love the Red Forest clip. The way the map opens up around the campfire feels really cozy, and "never seen you take it off once" made me laugh. Is that Blobknight? And is the launcher something you built for your own projects too?

replies.author: Ferniclestix
replies.body:
Yeah because my initial AI programming stuff was basically me asking gemini for snippets of code it meant I needed a way of patching it so I built a little app launcher to patch, do some AI stuff and organize my projects. 

but it was one of those early days setups. if I rebuilt it now i'd do it differently. I still use the launcher for backing things up and running my claude projects.
